breaking.headline: Attorney general finds no evidence Huang broke the law
breaking.fact: President Trump said today his attorney general confirmed the U.S. government has no evidence Jensen Huang engaged in “any unlawful conduct,” and Nvidia's board cited government input in reinstating him as CEO; Trump publicly praised the return as Nvidia soared more than 30%.

breaking.headline: Houston braces for the season's coldest air; first freeze possible Thanksgiving morning
breaking.fact: A reinforcing front late Tuesday brings the coldest air of the season to southeast Texas, with Houston's Thanksgiving-morning low near 38° and a possible first freeze across the Brazos Valley and Piney Woods; highs Thursday struggle to reach 60°.

breaking.headline: Record Thanksgiving travel week under way as Delta recovers
breaking.fact: AAA expects nearly 80 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles this week and TSA expects to screen 18.3 million people at airports; U.S. flights ran relatively normally Monday, with fewer than 40 canceled by midday on the East Coast, after Delta restored the system behind Sunday's delays.

breaking.headline: CrowdStrike tumbles on Zscaler deal as cybersecurity stocks split
breaking.fact: CrowdStrike shares fell about 8% after it agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, while Zscaler jumped about 15%; the deal, one of the largest cybersecurity mergers ever, is expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2028.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide inched up 0.04% in Paris to €187.66 — $205.28 at the ECB's Nov 23 reference rate of 1.0939. The industrial-gas giant barely moved while U.S. tech ripped higher, its usual defensive profile on full display. Its 7-day sparkline shows a slow, orderly drift in euros rather than any break. With no company news in play, the dollar price mostly tracks the euro from here.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic fell 3.5% to $85.80, the one big name left out of today's rally as valuation doubts linger. The stock is still in price discovery after Thursday's record debut — it opened at $111.50, closed day one at $97.17, then dropped 8.5% in Friday's rout. Swings like this are normal for a hot new listing with no trading history to anchor to. The $83 IPO price remains the level to watch underneath.

watchlist.name: SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up 0.01% to $91.60 — ballast on a day when almost everything else swung hard. The 1–3 month T-bill fund does exactly one job: it parks cash at a 4.04% distribution yield with essentially no price risk. Its latest distribution was $0.30849 a share, ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5. On days like today, this is the chip that lets the rest of the tape do whatever it wants.

watchlist.name: Alphabet (Google) Cl A
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet jumped 6.8% to $283.25 as the AI trade snapped back with the Magnificent Seven. The move recoups a chunk of last week's slide, when the stock fell with the broader tech rout despite no company-specific news. Google's cloud and AI positioning keeps it at the center of the AI-spending debate. Watch whether the bounce holds into Wednesday's PCE report, the next real test for the tape.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly rose 1.2% to $1,363.33, a quieter day for the drugmaker while tech stole the show. New research today showed semaglutide may help repair damaged kidneys — a class-wide read-through that keeps GLP-1 demand in focus. Lilly's weight-loss and diabetes franchises remain the growth engine. The stock sits near the top of the tape's defensive growth names, and today it acted like it.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere added 0.9% to $297.40 as energy lagged the rally and natural gas stayed in focus. The LNG exporter benefits from the Gazprom supply notice that lifted gas prices late last week, and U.S. export demand remains firm into winter. Cheniere's contracted volumes give it steadier cash flow than most energy names. With oil sliding on surplus fears today, gas-linked names held up better than crude producers.

watchlist.name: NVIDIA
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia soared 32.2% to $165.95 after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately — six days after saying it never would. The attorney general told Trump the government has no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct, and Trump praised the return. The stock is on pace for a record one-day market-value gain. The SEC probe and Huang's Dec 1 House interview remain open.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer ticked up 0.4% to $27.50, barely participating in a rally led by growth and tech. The drugmaker remains a yield-and-value name on this tape, with its dividend doing the heavy lifting while the pipeline rebuilds. Its 794.2-share position in the portfolio keeps it a steady income holding. Nothing company-specific moved it today; it simply tracked the broader market's drift higher.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 8.4% to $49.23 as space and growth names caught a strong bid in the relief rally. The launch company has been one of the tape's most volatile holdings, swinging hard with risk appetite in both directions. Today's gain recoups part of last week's selloff but leaves it well off recent highs. Watch for any fresh launch or contract news to set the next leg — the stock rarely sits still for long.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 1.8% to $8.20, a solid day for the mortgage REIT as the broad rally lifted financials. The stock's appeal is its dividend, which keeps paying while the shares trade in a narrow band. Mortgage REITs live and die on the rate curve, and the 10-year held near 4.93% today. With a December rate hike now fully priced in, the next read comes from Wednesday's PCE report.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SpaceX rose 5.2% to $134.39 as the AI and space trade rebounded together. Bernstein said today that SpaceX is about a decade ahead of rivals after Starship's first upper-stage catch on Nov 14, calling the recovery a key breakthrough. The firm also flagged rocket reusability as central to orbital data centers. Flight 17 hardware is already in cryo testing, with Ship 44 done and Booster 24 in test Sunday.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist gained 2.3% to $46.86 as banks joined the broad rally and the yield curve stayed steady. The regional bank benefits when rate fears ease, and today's 10-year near 4.93% kept that backdrop intact. Truist's dividend and southeastern footprint make it the tape's steady bank holding. The next catalyst is Wednesday's PCE report, which will shape what the Fed does at its Dec 8–9 meeting.

watchlist.name: United States Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony jumped 7.2% to $2.39, bouncing with the small-cap rally after last week's washout. The antimony miner remains a speculative bet on critical-mineral policy and domestic supply, with China export curbs as the long-run driver. Thin trading means moves like today's come fast in both directions. The bottom-watch tripwire stays in place: it needs a real base before it earns a bigger position.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy surged 9.5% to $5.81 as uranium names snapped back with the broader risk rally. The stock tracks the uranium price and nuclear-expansion headlines, both supportive longer term. Today's move recoups some of last week's losses but still leaves it well below its autumn highs. The gap watch stays paused until UEC starts popping on its own — today was a market move, not a uranium one.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 0.4% to $332.73, one of the few decliners as crude slid on surplus fears. Refining margins are the swing factor here, and cheaper crude can help them even as it pressures the oil price. The stock remains a long-term hold in the locked work-related sleeve, with 395 vested shares tradeable in the brokerage account. Energy was the day's weak spot; Valero simply went with its sector.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target Retirement 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV printed $27.75 as of Friday's close, down 2.1% from Thursday as the rout hit diversified funds too. Mutual funds price once a day after the close, so today's rebound won't show until tomorrow's NAV. The fund's glide path keeps it a set-and-forget holding for the 2035 horizon. Its next print should reflect today's broad rally across stocks and bonds alike.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Institutional 500 Index Trust
watchlist.blurb: The S&P-anchored estimate tracks the index's surge: $149.06 (est.), +4.94%. The estimate is built from the Nov 3 anchor — $155.58 when the S&P 500 closed 7,568.92 — and it has tracked the fund closely: Friday's actual close came in at $142.17 against a $142.04 estimate. Days like today are the anchor's best case, since it is the index. When the real NAV prints, expect it within a few dimes of this figure.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage Money Fund
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money market fund holds its stable $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 3.77% as published Nov 20. It is the sweep vehicle, where idle Schwab cash sits between CD purchases, and the plan is to sell it down whenever any account tops $1,000. Its yield trails the Treasury-only funds because it holds a broader mix. The comparison rate is VUSXX's 4.03% — the standing argument for keeping sweep balances small.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury Money Market Fund
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money market fund holds $1.00 with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03% as published Nov 20 — still the best yield in the cash class on this tape. Treasury-only holdings keep it as close to risk-free as a fund gets, and the 0.07% expense ratio leaves almost nothing on the table. It out-yields Schwab's sweep by about a quarter point. Every CD on the ladder has to beat this rate to earn its place.

weekInBrief.headline: Oil slides to two-month lows as surplus fears build
weekInBrief.body: Brent fell more than 6% and WTI nearly 5% on Monday as traders weighed a growing global supply surplus against the tanker attacks in the Gulf. January Brent touched its lowest since early September, while WTI hit its lowest since late August. The slide came even as Gulf shipping risks kept a premium in prices — supply, for now, is winning the argument.

weekInBrief.headline: Wednesday's PCE report looms as markets price a December hike
weekInBrief.body: Wednesday brings the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, with headline PCE expected at 3.8% and core at 3.2%, alongside revised GDP and the Fed's Beige Book — all two weeks before the Dec. 8–9 meeting. Markets now price a 25-basis-point hike as a near-certainty, and Governor Waller has openly floated 50. A hot print would test today's rally; a cool one could extend it.

weekInBrief.headline: Pending home sales hit a record low as mortgage rates climb
weekInBrief.body: October pending home sales fell 16.7% from a year ago to the lowest level since the National Association of Realtors began tracking the series in 2001, with all four regions down. Single-family permits dropped to their lowest in four years, and the 30-year mortgage rate ended a four-week slide at 7.28%. Builders' confidence fell to a 2012 low as price cuts and incentives hit post-Covid highs.

weekInBrief.headline: Semaglutide may help reverse chronic kidney disease
weekInBrief.body: The key ingredient in Ozempic repaired blood vessels, dampened inflammation and improved kidney function in patients with chronic kidney disease, researchers report in Nature Medicine. In kidney tissue samples, semaglutide increased blood flow, reduced scarring and switched off inflammatory genes while turning repair genes on. The disease affects an estimated 674 million people worldwide, and the finding adds kidney protection to the drug's growing list of benefits.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: UKMTO reported a tanker incident “involving a tanker and military forces” in the Gulf of Oman near Iran's port of Chabahar on Sunday evening, with no further details and no comment yet from the U.S. military. Iran's navy claimed on Nov. 21 and 22 that tankers hit mines east of the strait — claims no independent source has confirmed — while more than 14 tankers have assembled near Kharg Island as Tehran threatens to test the blockade. The Joint Maritime Information Center has logged seven tankers hit since Nov. 16, and President Trump said Sunday that Iran launched more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, all of them intercepted. On the oil itself, Kpler puts flows through the strait at about 9.5 million barrels a day over the 10 days through November 19, down from October's 12.2 million, while Iranian crude loadings remain at zero — the last Iranian cargoes discharged in China earlier this month, leaving no Iranian oil on the water outside the blockade.

space.headline: Bernstein: SpaceX is a decade ahead after Starship's first catch
space.body: Bernstein said today that SpaceX is about a decade ahead of its rivals in rocket recovery, calling Starship's first upper-stage catch on Nov. 14 a key breakthrough toward a fully reusable system. The 124-metre Starship flew 14 laps around Earth, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and was plucked from the sky by the launch tower's chopstick arms — though its Super Heavy booster was lost after its engines cut out early. Flight 17 hardware is already in cryo testing at Massey's, with Ship 44 finished and Booster 24 in test on Sunday.

space.headline: Ancient jaw reveals a modern-day mystery
space.body: La Trobe University researchers found a pronounced mandibular torus — a harmless bony ridge inside the lower jaw that dentists see often today — in a 2.1- to 2.8-million-year-old Australopithecus africanus fossil from Sterkfontein, South Africa. The Sts 52b specimen is one of the earliest and most pronounced examples of the trait in the hominin fossil record. Its cause in modern people is still unknown, with heavy chewing and tooth grinding among the suspects.

space.headline: Rembrandt's Night Watch is teeming with microbes
space.body: Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia researchers swabbing Rembrandt's 1642 masterpiece have catalogued a living microbiome on its surface — skin and soil bacteria, plus one puzzler, Microbacterium saccharophilum, first found at a Japanese sugar refinery in 2013. Sixty samples from 10 areas are planned, with 20 microbes identified so far and another 10 still incubating. The census is part of Operation Night Watch, the conservation project running since 2019.

space.headline: Roman cup in a 2,000-year-old tomb maps an ancient exchange network
space.body: A four-year excavation of Tomb 160 in Mongolia — the largest Xiongnu tomb found in the country, nearly 240 feet long — recovered 413 artifacts, including a glass cup believed to be of Roman origin, a silver horse-harness pendant and 15 jade pieces modeled after Han funerary goods. The haul shows the Xiongnu linked to a trade network stretching from Rome to the Korean Peninsula. DNA analysis of teeth and hair from the coffin is planned to identify the tomb's occupant.

apod.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
apod.explanation: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulate biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient's risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments.
